ui.sottotitolo: Viareggio workshop · AISI 316 stainless steel since 1999
ui.descrizioneTavola: Animated isometric drawing of the Fontealta workshop: twelve steps, from the six-metre steel bar to the packed shower column.
ui.animazioniRidotte: Animations reduced by your system settings
ui.tocca: Tap a department to see it up close

schede.testo: It all starts with six-metre stainless steel bars, made only in Europe. Every raw tube is inspected and read: the laser marking gives diameter, wall thickness, heat number, AISI 316 code, batch and date. Traceability starts here.

The bars are cut in half: three metres of developed length, the size of Boss and Boss Wide, with no offcuts. On the Twiggy the cut is angled at 30° while the tube is still straight, so that once the column is bent the head sits parallel to the ground.

schede.dati: 3 mm wall · bronze and aluminium mandrel
schede.testo: A moving mandrel in bronze and aluminium alloy runs inside the tube, following the bending machine and keeping the section round. The elasticity of steel changes from one heat to the next, so the angle is recalibrated by hand for every batch: bend, measure, correct.
Raw steel is porous, and rust starts in the pores. That is why the tube is first worked by hand with abrasive papers, from the coarsest grit to the finest, and with the flap disc grinder.

Belt and flap brush machines close the pores. On the smooth surface chromium oxide forms everywhere and seals it, even against sea salt. From here the piece takes its finish: Super Mirror, brushed or painted.

The painting is done in Viareggio by the painters of megayachts and Carnival floats. Then the piece dries in the air for fourteen days: paint that is not baked stays elastic and does not crack when the metal expands in the sun. That is two of the five weeks of production.

schede.dati: 5-axis waterjet · almandine · flanges up to 300 mm
schede.testo: For the heaviest structural components the five-axis waterjet comes in: water and almandine sand at 5200 bar cold-cut flanges up to 300 mm thick, including for the welded supports on cruise ship decks.

schede.dati: CNC machining centres · AISI 316, not brass
schede.testo: A little further on, CNC centres mill the internal bodies of the timed taps, and every mechanical part, from solid AISI 316. Meanwhile the column is drilled one hole at a time, made to measure for each customer.

schede.dati: Flexible hoses · fittings to the millimetre
schede.testo: On one side of the department, skilled hands fit the internal plumbing: flexible hoses and small, complex fittings, each one demanding millimetre precision.
On the other side, TIG welding consolidates the largest external structures. It is the slowest method, and it is the one that holds.

schede.dati: Laser marking · hydraulic test on every column
schede.testo: The handles receive the laser marking that authenticates the piece. Every column then passes hydraulic testing and quality control before leaving the department.
The column is wrapped in a peelable protective film, closed in a soft bag and then in shock-proof packing. From half a raw bar to a column that leaves for every corner of the world.

apertura.testo: This illustration follows the story filmed in the Viareggio workshop: a six-metre bar, cut in half, becomes two shower columns. Every person, machine and drop of water is drawn by code.

sottotitoli: Every high-end shower column begins long before the design,
it begins with a rigorous choice of raw material.
It all starts with massive stainless steel bars, 6 metres long,
made exclusively in Europe.
Nothing is left to chance.
Every single raw tube is inspected and laser marked,
diameter, wall thickness, heat number, AISI 316 code,
batch and exact production date.
Complete traceability from the very first moment.
No waste, no excess.
The 6-metre bars are cut exactly in half,
3 metres of developed length,
the perfect size for iconic models such as the BOSS and BOSS-WIDE lines.
But in some series, like the Twiggy, the cut already holds a secret.
It is made at a 30-degree angle, before the tube is even worked.
So when the column takes on its bent shape,
the cut will sit perfectly parallel to the ground.
Cold bending a steel tube with a wall over 3 mm, without deforming it,
takes rare skill.
The secret is a moving mandrel in a special bronze and aluminium alloy.
Inserted in the tube, it follows the bending machine and keeps the section round,
stopping the metal from collapsing as the inner wall compresses and the outer wall stretches.
Yet technology alone is not enough.
The elasticity of steel changes imperceptibly from one heat to the next.
That is why, at the start of every batch, skilled hands recalibrate the bend angle, one at a time.
People often wonder how these showers never rust,
not even when exposed to sea salt.
With the same material, the secret of corrosion resistance is a flawless finish.
Raw steel is naturally porous.
So the tube is worked by hand with abrasive papers of increasing grit.
Then specialised machines take over, with belts and flap brushes,
which close the pores for good.
This meticulous sanding lets the chromium oxide wrap the entire surface,
sealing it without leaving a single weak point.
From this polished base, the product takes on its final look,
a Super Mirror finish, brushed or painted.
And for the painting, natural drying is the choice here,
which extends production time to as much as 5 weeks.
The reason?
Paint that is not heat-dried keeps a remarkable elasticity.
It does not crack when the metal expands in the sun,
and withstands temperatures from minus 20 to over 60 degrees.
For the heaviest structural components, steel meets the force of water.
A 5-axis waterjet combines a jet of water with almandine sand,
and, at a pressure of 5200 bar, cold-cuts flanges up to 300 mm thick,
even producing the welded supports for cruise ship decks.
A little further on, CNC machining centres mill the internal bodies of the timed taps from solid,
and every mechanical part,
while the column’s structure takes shape hole by hole, made to measure for each customer.
Assembly reveals the harmony of a close-knit team.
On one side, skilled hands prepare the tiny, complex internal plumbing systems,
where every fitting demands millimetre precision.
On the other, the external work and the powerful V-radius TIG welds
shape imposing structures.
We are at the end of the journey.
The handles receive an elegant laser marking that authenticates the piece.
Once it has passed strict hydraulic and quality tests,
the column is wrapped in a peelable protective film
and protected in its shock-proof packing.
From a raw metal bar to the fluid lines of a design made to stand the test of time,
the masterpiece is ready to travel to every corner of the world.
